name: Software passkey for test tools
plain: Test tools can add a pretend passkey device to a browser so sign in flows run without hardware.
meaning: The WebAuthn spec defines a WebDriver extension for virtual authenticators. Chrome exposes it through the DevTools Protocol WebAuthn domain and Selenium and Playwright expose it to scripts. A test or agent can register and use passkeys with no phone or security key. A site cannot call this from a page; it is a tool level control.

web.api: WebDriver Virtual Authenticator commands; CDP WebAuthn.addVirtualAuthenticator, addCredential, setUserVerified

access.prompt_ui: None; only the driver can turn it on
access.revocation: Close the session or remove the authenticator
access.iframe: Applies to the whole browser session
steps: Test tool starts a virtual authenticator in the browser
Tool adds or accepts credentials through the protocol
Page runs the normal WebAuthn calls

chrome.note: Through the DevTools Protocol WebAuthn domain and ChromeDriver

firefox.note: Driver support varies; verify for your version

safari.note: Driver support varies; verify for your version

fields.name: hasUserVerification
fields.range: whether the virtual device passes user checks

limits.headline: Lets tests and agents use passkeys without a phone
limits.user_action: None. A developer turns it on from the test tool
can: Create a software authenticator in tests
Register and sign in with passkeys in CI
Check a sign in flow end to end
cannot: Be used by a normal web page
Fool a site that checks attestation against known devices
Replace a person's approval in real accounts
Work on a locked down browser
limits.reach_label: A test device the driver controls
limits.differs: It is a driver feature, not a web API. Sites that require hardware attestation reject the virtual device.

story.what_it_is: A pretend security key that a test tool plugs in so sign in tests can run on any computer.

marketing.name: Emulate authenticators
marketing.pitch: Docs show how DevTools adds a virtual authenticator to test passkeys.

story.for_you: You never see it. It is a tool for testers. It lets teams check that passkey sign in works without handing out hardware.
story.for_makers: Use it for tests only. In agent products, a virtual authenticator must not stand in for a person's approval on a real account.

use_cases.example: A QA team tests passkey sign in in CI with a virtual authenticator.
A security team tests how a site handles invalid passkey answers.
A bank tests its sign in pages without hardware keys.
A platform team checks a passkey rollout against many browsers.
A store tests passkey checkout on staging.
A SaaS team runs passkey tests on every release.

risks: Could be used to script real sign ins if misused

technical_bounds: Not allowed by sites that check attestation

abuse: Scripted sign ins by agents that should hand off to a person

history.change: WebAuthn domain added to the DevTools Protocol and ChromeDriver
